correctness.rationale: The two means use unordered distinct pairs and their separate denominators. The edge-cut contributions count precisely the pairs whose unique paths cross that edge, so the stated integer sign test is valid. I independently generated unlabelled trees by attaching a leaf at every vertex of every previous-order representative and deduplicating by the minimum rooted parenthesis code over all roots. The rooted code is complete by induction on the multiset of child codes, and deleting any leaf from a tree shows generation is exhaustive. Direct pair distances (not edge-cut sums) gave nonnegative minima for every order 2–14; at 14 the minimum was 1/52. At 15 there were 7,741 classes, exactly three negative, and exactly one attaining -1/10. The negative classes match canonical codes of B_7,7, B_8,6 and B_9,5 with (leaf count, ordinary sum, terminal sum) = (8,378,98), (9,336,112), (10,296,126), giving -1/10, -4/45, -2/105. This includes order 2, where the samples coincide. Replay: python3 /workspace/repro/record4.py; output /workspace/repro/record4.out. This independently covers the bounded claim without NetworkX and provides no classification at later orders.

value.rationale: The normalization makes comparison of terminal and ordinary mean distances a natural deterministic question raised by random-tree work.
